Subject: Post-call: Encryption & KMS requirements (Acme Corp)

Hi Elena / Jasper —

Thanks for the call this morning — great to meet the security and infra teams. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

Summary from call:
- You are evaluating Redwood for chat/embedding endpoints for a customer-facing product that handles PII.
- Primary requirements: encryption in-transit and at-rest, option for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS or HSM), strict logging/audit controls, and data residency in us-west region.

What Redwood provides (high-level):
- TLS 1.2+ for in-transit encryption for all API traffic.
- At-rest encryption by default; option to use customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault or bring-your-own HSM for Private deployments.
- Audit logs, access logs, and token-level traces available in the Console (can be exported to your SIEM).

Ask / next steps:
1) Please confirm the KMS model you prefer (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM) and whether the keys must be inside your VPC/HSM.
2) Any specific retention window for logs and inference inputs we should plan for?
3) Would you like a technical deep-dive with our infra team (Vivek) to walk through KMS integration and key rotation?

Attaching: redwood-kms-options.pdf (high-level options) and your copy of the acme-encryption-requirements.pdf from the call.

I'll loop in Vivek for any technical followups. Happy to set up a dedicated session early next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync: 

1) KMS model: We prefer customer-managed keys in our AWS account (AWS KMS CMKs) for the MVP. For long-term, the security team wants the option for an HSM-backed key that they control (FIPS 140-2/3) if we move to private deployment.

2) Key residency: Keys must remain in our AWS account/us-west-2. Any integration should not require exporting key material out of our account.

3) At-rest encryption: Confirm that Redwood can use our CMKs to encrypt model artifacts and persistent caches for our tenant. Also need details on how key rotation is handled and whether rotation impacts availability.

4) In-transit: TLS is expected. Please confirm support for mutual TLS (mTLS) for service-to-service communication (our preference for backend-to-backend).

5) Logging and audit: We need proof of access logs for key operations (encrypt/decrypt requests), and audit trails for who/what rotated keys. Can we route logs to our CloudWatch/S3 or a SIEM? Retention requested: 1 year for access logs, 3 years for audit logs.

6) Performance: Any latency/throughput implications when using CMKs vs Redwood-managed keys? If possible, share data or benchmarks.

Can Vivek or Rishi provide written answers to the above (and any docs) before we escalate to procurement? Also please include any required ATO / SOC2 artifacts.

Elena
Sr. Security Engineer, Acme Corp
elena.torres@acme-corp.com

Hi Elena — thanks, excellent list. I've captured these as action items and looped in Vivek and Rishi. High-level answers below; Vivek / Rishi will follow up with details and docs.

Quick answers:
- KMS model / residency: We support using your AWS KMS CMKs in your account (cross-account grant model for hosted deployments) and can integrate with customer-managed KMS in Private deployments where key material stays in your account/HSM. No key material is exported by Redwood.
- At-rest: Yes, we can encrypt tenant data and persistent caches with your CMK. Rotation: we support scheduled rotation and can perform re-encryption without downtime in most cases; we'll provide the rotation playbook.
- mTLS: Supported for dedicated/private deployments; for hosted API we provide mTLS for backend-to-backend customers via private endpoints/VPC peering (we can detail this).
- Logs & audit: Access logs and KMS operation logs can be exported to your CloudWatch/S3 or forwarded to a SIEM. We can meet the retention windows you specified.
- Performance: Using customer-managed KMS for envelope encryption adds minimal overhead (single extra KMS call per key wrap/unwrap). For high-throughput scenarios we recommend using envelope keys with a short-lived data key cache to minimize KMS requests. We'll share benchmark numbers.

Attaching: redwood-kms-faq.pdf with initial technical notes and a link to our SOC2 and encryption docs in the related links.

Proposed next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Vivek (infra) and Rishi (solutions) — 60 minutes.
2) Share SOC2 artefacts & encryption whitepaper (we'll send a signed NDA if needed).
3) Confirm KMS approach (AWS CMK for MVP), then we can generate a mutual action plan for procurement.

Which times next week work for your team?

Best,
Marissa

Quick technical note / follow-up: 

- Cross-account AWS KMS model: We'll ask Acme to create a CMK in your account and grant Redwood's service principal a decrypt/encrypt grant scoped to the key. We use envelope encryption: per-tenant data key (DEK) generated and wrapped with your CMK. DEKs are cached in memory for short windows to avoid repeated KMS calls.
- HSM/private keys: For Private deployments we can integrate with your HSM using either KMIP or provider-specific HSM integrations; key material never leaves your HSM.
- Rotation: Rotation is handled by creating a new CMK version + re-wrap; for large data sets re-encryption is done lazily on access to avoid downtime; we will run a pre-migration plan if you require eager re-encryption.
- Audit logs: Redwood will emit KMS-related events; we can stream these to your CloudWatch or S3 via cross-account logging or push to your SIEM over TLS.

I'll prepare a short ops-runbook and benchmark notes (latency microbenchmarks for KMS unwrap) and drop them into the Drive link Marissa shared. Happy to present on the deep-dive.

-Vivek
